title: AMA releases governance framework for agentic AI in healthcare
key_facts: The American Medical Association released a framework of four questions for assessing AI agents used in clinical tasks, including what the agent may do and who is responsible
Agentic AI can do multi-step tasks without human oversight, so an error could harm a patient before a clinician steps in
Survey of 250 US healthcare leaders: about 28% have deployed agentic AI, 44% are piloting it
72% say agentic tools are sometimes used without IT approval
47 states introduced over 250 healthcare AI bills in 2025 (Manatt)
No substantive federal AI regulation; industry groups provide guidance
quote_evidence: "As AI capabilities advance, evidence, authority, oversight and accountability must remain aligned in service of better patient care," the framework states.
In a recent survey of 250 U.S. healthcare leaders, about 28% said their organization has already deployed agentic AI tools, and 44% reported conducting pilots or proof-of-concept projects.
Health AI is evolving so quickly that regulations are struggling to keep up.
why_it_matters_hint: Guidance arrives while hospitals deploy AI agents faster than rules or oversight.
notes: The four questions are not listed in the text retrieved; only two are paraphrased.
